sso_guide.title: How to set up Microsoft Entra ID
sso_guide.dialog_title: Connect Microsoft Entra ID, step by step
sso_guide.intro: You need an Entra ID administrator account. The whole procedure takes about five minutes.
sso_guide.s1: Open the **Microsoft Entra admin center** > **App registrations** > **New registration**.
sso_guide.s2: Under **Supported account types** choose **Single tenant only**.
sso_guide.s3: Set the Redirect URI platform to **Web**, paste the URI shown below and click **Register**.
sso_guide.s5: In **Certificates & secrets** create a **Client secrets** entry and copy its **Value**.
sso_guide.b1: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to **App registrations** and click **New registration**.
sso_guide.t2: Name the app and choose Single tenant
sso_guide.b2: Enter a name your colleagues will recognise, for example **AION Agent**. Under **Supported account types** select **Single tenant only**: the first option, followed by the name of your organisation. Do not choose the multitenant or personal-account options. AION signs users in against your own directory only.
sso_guide.b3: In **Redirect URI (optional)** choose the **Web** platform and paste the address below. Then click **Register**.
sso_guide.cap1: Registration form: the numbers match the steps above.
sso_guide.t4: Copy the application and tenant IDs
sso_guide.b4: The new app opens on **Overview**. Copy **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID** and paste them into the matching fields of this page.
sso_guide.b5: In the app menu open **Certificates & secrets**, select the **Client secrets** tab and click **New client secret**. Add a description such as AION, keep the suggested expiry (180 days) or pick another one, then click **Add**.
sso_guide.cap2: Certificates & secrets: add the client secret.
sso_guide.b6: Copy the **Value** column right away: Microsoft shows it only once. Do not copy **Secret ID**. Paste it into the **Client secret** field of this page.
sso_guide.warn: When the secret expires, Microsoft sign-in stops working until you create a new one and enter it here. Note the expiry date in your calendar.
sso_guide.b7: Click **Save and verify with my account** and sign in with your Microsoft account in the pop-up. When the configuration is validated, use **Set as default** to make Microsoft the sign-in method.
sso_guide.shots_note: Screenshots come from the Italian portal; labels follow the language of your Microsoft account.
sso_guide.alt1: Microsoft Entra: Register an application form
sso_guide.alt2: Microsoft Entra: Add a client secret panel
sso_guide.btn_save_verify: Save and verify with my account

sso_guide_google.title: How to set up Google sign-in
sso_guide_google.dialog_title: Connect Google sign-in, step by step
sso_guide_google.intro: You need a Google account that can create projects in Google Cloud. The procedure takes about ten minutes.
sso_guide_google.s1: Open the Google Cloud Console and create a project (or pick an existing one).
sso_guide_google.s2: In **Google Auth Platform** click **Get started** and fill in app name, support email, audience and contact email.
sso_guide_google.s3: Open **Clients** > **Create client** and choose **Web application** as application type.
sso_guide_google.s4: Paste the URI shown below into **Authorized redirect URIs** and click **Create**.
sso_guide_google.s5: Copy **Client ID** and **Client secret**: the secret is shown only once.
sso_guide_google.b1: Open the Google Cloud Console and create a new project with **New project**, or select one you already use. Enter a **Project name** such as **AION Agent** and click **Create**.
sso_guide_google.b2: Search for **Google Auth Platform** in the top search bar and open it. If it says the platform is not configured yet, click **Get started**.
sso_guide_google.b3: Type an app name (for example **AION Agent**) and choose the **User support email**. Users see them on the Google consent screen. Click **Next**.
sso_guide_google.b4: Pick **Internal** if your company uses Google Workspace: only your organisation's accounts can sign in and no Google verification is needed. Pick **External** otherwise. In that case the app starts in test mode and only users you add under **Audience** > Test users can sign in. Click **Next**.
sso_guide_google.t5: Add a contact email and finish
sso_guide_google.b5: Enter an email address in **Contact information** and click **Next**. Then accept the Google API Services user data policy, click **Continue** and finally **Create**.
sso_guide_google.b6: In the left menu open **Clients** and click **Create client**.
sso_guide_google.b7: Choose **Web application** as application type and give the client a name, for example **AION Agent**. Under **Authorized redirect URIs** click **Add URI**, paste the address below and click **Create**.
sso_guide_google.t8: Copy Client ID and Client secret
sso_guide_google.b8: Google shows both values in the **OAuth client created** dialog. Copy them and paste them into **Client ID** and **Client secret** on this page.
sso_guide_google.warn: The client secret cannot be shown again after you close the dialog. If you lose it, you must create a new one from the client page.
sso_guide_google.b9: Click **Save and verify with my account** and sign in with your Google account in the pop-up. When the configuration is validated, use **Set as default** to make Google the sign-in method.
sso_guide_google.c2: Google Auth Platform overview: start the configuration.
sso_guide_google.c3: App information: app name and support email.
sso_guide_google.c4: Audience: Internal for Workspace, External otherwise.
sso_guide_google.c6: Accept the policy, continue and create.
sso_guide_google.c8: Client form: type, name and redirect URI.
sso_guide_google.c9: OAuth client created: copy both values (hidden here).
sso_guide_google.shots_note: Screenshots come from the Italian portal; labels follow the language of your Google account. Credentials and email addresses in the images are hidden.

stt.model_hint: The model runs on this server: audio is never sent outside. Larger models handle accents, technical terms and noisy audio better, but they are slower and use more memory.

tiny.title: Minimal
tiny.description: About 75 MB. Very fast but inaccurate, especially in Italian: only for testing or servers with very little memory.

base.title: Light
base.description: About 145 MB. Fast and undemanding: fine for short voice messages and clean audio, but gets names and uncommon words wrong more often.

small.title: Standard
small.description: About 460 MB on disk and 1 GB of memory while in use. A good balance between quality and speed in Italian.

medium.title: Advanced
medium.description: About 1.5 GB. More accurate on accents, technical terms and noisy audio, but clearly slower and uses more memory.

large-v3-turbo.title: Large, optimized
large-v3-turbo.description: About 1.6 GB. Quality close to the largest model in less time; needs a powerful processor and a few GB of memory.

large-v3.title: Highest quality
large-v3.description: About 3 GB. The most accurate, but very slow on a processor: long recordings need several passes. Only for dedicated servers.

stt.custom_model: Set manually in the server configuration.
stt.not_installed: This model is not on the server yet. Download it now: otherwise it will be downloaded during the first transcription, which may not finish in time.
stt.downloading_hint: The model is downloading to the server. Wait until it finishes before saving: saving may restart the service and interrupt the download.
stt.language_hint: The language spoken in the recordings. Setting it is faster and more accurate than detecting it; the agent can still pick another language for a single file.

auto.title: Detect automatically
auto.description: The model guesses the language of each file. Useful with mixed languages, a little slower and less reliable on short clips.

language.custom_description: Value set manually in the server configuration.

stt.beam_hint: For each sentence the model weighs several possible versions of the text and picks the most likely one. Comparing more helps with ambiguous words and proper names, but slows transcription down.

1.title: Fast
1.description: Always picks the most likely word without comparing alternatives. The quickest, with a few more mistakes on similar or unclear words. Useful with slow processors or many simultaneous conversations.

3.title: Balanced
3.description: Compares 3 versions of the text: a compromise between speed and accuracy.

5.title: Accurate
5.description: Compares 5 versions of the text, the model’s standard setting. The most accurate, but the slowest of the three.

beam.custom_description: Value set manually in the server configuration.

stt.apply_note: Changes apply to conversations started after saving. Every conversation that transcribes audio loads its own copy of the model into memory: with many simultaneous users, prefer a smaller model.

page.title: WhatsApp
page.subtitle: Connect your company’s WhatsApp Business number so colleagues can message the agent straight from WhatsApp.
page.config_desc: Your Meta app credentials, the webhook and channel activation.
page.users_desc: Colleagues who linked their WhatsApp from the chat settings.

summary.title: How to connect WhatsApp
summary.s1: Create a **Business** type Meta app and add the **WhatsApp** product.
summary.s2: Register the company number in **WhatsApp Manager** and copy the **Phone Number ID** and **WABA ID**.
summary.s3: Generate a **permanent token** from a system user and copy the **App secret**.
summary.s4: Paste the values here, generate the **verify token**, save and set up the **webhook** on Meta.
summary.s5: Click **Verify** and, once every check is green, **enable the channel**.

guide.dialog_title: Connect WhatsApp Business, step by step
guide.intro: You need an admin account on the company’s Meta business portfolio and a phone number that is not already active on WhatsApp. It takes about 20 minutes, plus Meta’s verification times.
guide.b1: Sign in to **business.facebook.com** with the company account and create or pick the company’s **business portfolio**. **Business verification** is not required to get started, but it is recommended: without it Meta applies lower limits on conversations and the display name.
guide.b2: On **developers.facebook.com/apps** click **Create app**, enter a name and a contact email, choose the use case **Connect with customers through WhatsApp** and link the app to the business portfolio from step 1. Review the summary and click **Create app**.
guide.b3: In the app open **Use cases** and click **Customize** on the WhatsApp use case, then go to **Step 2. Production setup** and click **Add phone number**. Enter the **display name** colleagues will see and the business category, then the number, verify it with the code you receive by **SMS** and create the **Messaging account**.
guide.warn3: The number must not already be active on WhatsApp, neither on the regular app nor on WhatsApp Business. If it is, delete that account from the phone first.
guide.b4: Once the number is registered, **Step 2. Production setup** shows its **Phone number ID** and the **Messaging account ID** (WABA ID) right under it: copy both. They are also listed in **WhatsApp** > **API Setup**.
guide.b5: In **Business settings** > **Users** > **System users** click **Add** and create a system user with the **Admin** role. With **Assign assets** give it the app from step 2 (full control, **Manage app**) and the WhatsApp account from step 3. Then click **Generate token**, pick the app, expiry **Never** and the **whatsapp_business_management** and **whatsapp_business_messaging** permissions.
guide.warn5: Meta shows the token only once: copy it right away. Don’t use the temporary token on the API Setup page, it expires after 24 hours.
guide.b6: In the Meta app open **App settings** > **Basic**, click **Show** next to **App secret** and copy it. AION uses it to check the signature of every webhook.
guide.b7: Come back to this page and fill in **WABA ID**, **Phone Number ID**, **Access token** and **App secret**. Click **Generate** next to **Verify token**, then **Save**.
guide.t8: Set up the webhook on Meta
guide.b8: In the Meta app open **WhatsApp** > **Configuration** and, in the **Webhook** section, click **Edit**. Paste the **Callback URL** and **Verify token** below, then click **Verify and save**. On the same page, under **Webhook fields**, subscribe to the **messages** field.
guide.no_token: Generate the verify token from the panel first (step 7).
guide.b9: In **WhatsApp Manager** add a **payment method**: each number gets 1,000 free service messages per month, after that they are charged. **Publishing the app (Live mode) is optional**: the channel already works with the app showing **Not published** in the **Publish** item of the left menu, so you can skip it. Finally come back to AION, click **Verify** and, once every check is green, **Enable channel**.
guide.shots_note: Screenshots come from Meta’s Italian interface, with emails, phone numbers, IDs and tokens masked. Meta changes its interface often, so labels may look slightly different.
guide.cap_app_details: Enter the app name and the contact email, then click Next.
guide.cap_app_use_case: Under Business messaging, pick “Connect with customers through WhatsApp”.
guide.cap_app_business_portfolio: Link the app to the company’s business portfolio.
guide.cap_app_review_create: Review the summary and click Create app.
guide.cap_use_cases_customize: In the app’s Use cases, click Customize on the WhatsApp use case.
guide.cap_add_phone_number: Open Step 2. Production setup and click Add phone number.
guide.cap_whatsapp_profile: Enter the display name and pick the business category.
guide.cap_phone_verify: Choose SMS to receive the verification code.
guide.cap_messaging_account: Create the Messaging account that will hold the number.
guide.cap_registered_ids: The registered number shows its Messaging account ID (WABA ID) and Phone number ID: copy them.
guide.cap_system_users: In Business settings > Users > System users, click Add.
guide.cap_system_user_create: Name the system user and give it the Admin role.
guide.cap_system_user_assign: Select the new system user and click Assign assets.
guide.cap_assign_assets_dialog: Select the app and turn on Manage app (full access).
guide.cap_assets_assigned: With the app assigned, click Generate token.
guide.cap_token_created: Copy the token now: Meta shows it only once.
guide.cap_temp_token: The token on the API Setup page is temporary and expires after 24 hours: don’t use it.
guide.cap_app_secret: In App settings > Basic, click Show next to App secret.
guide.cap_app_unpublished: The app can stay “Not published”: publishing is optional and the channel already works without it.

verify.desc: Checks the token, the number and the webhook on Meta, then enable the channel.
verify.not_configured: Save the credentials to be able to verify.
